basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 1.' and it opens 'Vers. 1. Egressa est Dina. Allegorice Dina significat | animam sua studia negligentem, et'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 1. Egressa est Dina. Allegorice Dina significat | animam sua studia negligentem, et aliorum facta studiosius inquirentem. Quasi enim egreditur ad videndas mulieres, cum sua intima projicit et in exterioribus occupatur. Mox ergo ut ita egreditur a Sichem, id est a diabolo, opprimitur et incestatur. Unde bene Dina judicium istud interpretatur. Istud enim est judicium, ut, quia sponte se negligens evagatur, mox a diabolo corrumpatur.
